prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live browsing access, so I can’t look up current contractor listings or confirm who’s available right now in Joplin — but I can help you find a reliable contractor and avoid problems. If you tell me the job type (kitchen, bathroom, whole‑house remodel, roof, electrical, plumbing, etc.), budget, and timeline I can give more specific questions and a short RFP you can send to prospects.

Immediate steps to find a reliable Joplin contractor
1. Start with these local and vetting resources
   - Google Maps & Reviews — search “home remodel Joplin MO” and sort by ratings and recent reviews.  
   - Better Business Bureau (BBB) — check ratings, complaints, and how they were handled.  
   - Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack/Houzz — for vetted pros and customer photos.  
   - Local groups — Nextdoor, Joplin Facebook community groups, and the Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce for referrals.  
   - City/County building department — confirm the contractor pulls proper permits and check for any complaints filed locally.

2. Verify credentials
   - Ask for proof of liability insurance and worker’s comp (get certificate of insurance).  
   - For specialty work (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) verify state or local trade licensing.  
   - Get company business registration/contractor license if applicable and ask how long they’ve operated in Joplin.

3. Get multiple written bids
   - Obtain at least 2–3 detailed, written estimates that list labor, materials, allowances, timeline, and payment schedule.  
   - Make sure bids are apples-to-apples (same materials, scope).

4. Ask for references and recent work
   - Request 3 recent local references and call them about punctuality, communication, cleanliness, quality, change orders, and final billing.  
   - Ask to see photos of completed jobs or visit a current job site (with permission).

5. Contract checklist
   - Detailed scope of work, start & completion dates, milestone/retention payment schedule.  
   - Specifications for materials/brands/colors and allowances for choices.  
   - Change order process (how changes are priced and approved).  
   - Warranty on workmanship and materials and who handles manufacturer warranties.  
   - Payment method and lien waiver requirements.  
   - Statement about who obtains permits and conducts inspections.

6. Red flags
   - Asks for large upfront cash payment (>10–20%).  
   - No written contract or vague scope.  
   - Poor or no references, or lots of unresolved BBB complaints.  
   - Pressure to sign immediately or offers an unusually low bid without detail.

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email/RFP you can send to contractors;
- Provide a short checklist to compare estimates side‑by‑side;
- Recommend specific questions to ask based on your project type;
- Help evaluate 2–3 bids if you paste them here.

Tell me the project type, rough budget, and whether you prefer licensed specialty trades or a general contractor who manages subs, and I’ll tailor the next steps and sample questions.
